name: Steel Dynamics
description: Steel Dynamics is a US steelmaker that melts scrap in electric arc furnaces, so its profit is the gap between steel prices and scrap cost rather than iron-ore economics. It also owns a large scrap-metal recycling business (OmniSource) that feeds its own mills, a steel joist and deck fabricator (New Millennium) for non-residential buildings, and a new flat-rolled aluminum mill that is still losing money (a $173M operating loss in 2025). Steel Operations was 74% of 2025 sales (before eliminations) and 97% of segment operating income. 2025 shipments were a record 13.7 million tons on new value-added coating lines at Sinton, Texas and Heartland, while fabrication sales fell 20% on lower prices.

gics.note: Sector and sub-industry from Wikipedia 'List of S&P 500 companies' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_S%26P_500_companies, read 2026-09-30); that list does not show the industry group or industry, so those are null.

businessLines.name: Steel Operations
businessLines.how: Sells steel by the ton at market spot and contract prices to construction, automotive, manufacturing and energy customers; profit is the spread between steel prices and scrap cost (metallic raw materials are about 55% to 65% of mill manufacturing cost).
businessLines.description: Electric arc furnace flat roll mills (Butler, Columbus, Sinton), structural and rail, engineered bar, Roanoke Bar and Steel of West Virginia, plus steel coating lines; record 13.7 million tons shipped in 2025 (12.3 million excluding intra-segment).

businessLines.name: Metals Recycling Operations
businessLines.how: Buys scrap and sells processed ferrous and nonferrous metal by the ton; margin is the buy-sell spread; most output is sold to Steel Operations at intersegment prices ($2,304M intersegment of $4,346M).
businessLines.description: Ferrous and nonferrous scrap processing, transport, marketing and brokerage (OmniSource); supplies its own mills and sells to others.

businessLines.name: Steel Fabrication Operations
businessLines.how: Fabricated steel products sold per project to non-residential builders from a backlog; price follows the cost of steel purchased (about two-thirds of production cost).
businessLines.description: New Millennium Building Systems: steel joists, joist girders and steel deck for non-residential construction in the US and northern Mexico.

businessLines.how: Sells flat-rolled aluminum by the ton to packaging, auto and building customers; still a start-up with fixed costs above sales.
businessLines.description: Aluminum Dynamics flat-rolled aluminum mill (Columbus, Mississippi) plus Aluminum Dynamics of Mexico recycling and rolling, ramping up.
